prerequisites: It is recommended to have completed the technological baccalaureate.

learning_outcomes.text: Ability to understand and apply the basic principles of general chemistry, organic and inorganic chemistry and their applications in engineering.
That students have developed those skills necessary to undertake further studies with a high degree of autonomy.
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects that enables them to learn new methods and theories, and provides them with versatility to adapt to new situations.
Ability to apply knowledge in practice.
Ability to work in a team.
Aptitude for oral and written communication in the native language.
Capacity for autonomous and deep learning.
Competence in the critical contextualization of knowledge, establishing interrelationships with social, economic and environmental problems, local and/or global.
Competence in the application of ethical principles related to sustainability values in personal and professional behavior.

The objective of the course is to provide the student with a solid general formation on the structure of matter and its chemical transformations. This general formation should serve as a basis for the student to study and understand the behavior and processing of materials. Likewise, they should know the methodology for solving chemical problems within Industrial Engineering.

syllabus_topics: Chemistry as an experimental science. Course organization.

Atomic theory and chemical bonding. Atomic masses. Isotopes. Concept of mole and Avogadro's constant. The periodic table. Electrons in the atom. Quantum theory. Atomic models. Orbitals. Electronic configurations. Chemical compounds. Chemical bonding.

Main states of aggregation of matter. States of aggregation of matter. Changes of state. Intermolecular forces. Van der Waals forces. Hydrogen bond. Types of substances. Solids and their properties. Liquids and their properties. Gases and their properties.
The chemical language. Atomic symbol, periodic table, oxidation state number. Formulation. Nomenclature.
Chemical reactions and equations. Chemical reaction. Chemical equations. Stoichiometry. Limiting reactant. Reaction yield. Reaction intermediates.
Reactions in aqueous solution. Types of reactions in aqueous solution. Precipitation reactions. Acid-base reactions. Redox reactions.
Factors controlling chemical reactions. Thermochemistry. Chemical kinetics. Chemical equilibrium. Solubility and acid-base equilibria. Entropy and spontaneity of chemical reactions.

Electrochemistry. Electrode potentials and their measurement. Standard electrode potentials. Cell potential, Gibbs free energy change and equilibrium constant. Cell potential as a function of concentration. Batteries and cells. Corrosion: unwanted voltaic cells. Electrolysis.
Carbon chemistry. Introduction to organic compounds and their structures. Families of organic compounds.
Polymers and new materials in the chemical industry. Introduction. Types of polymers. Types of polymerization.
teaching_methods: Lectures (magistral expositions) with audiovisual support and blackboard use, fostering debate.

assessment_methods.method: Continuous assessment activities (assignments, problem solving, MOODLE questionnaires)

assessment_rules: The final grade is based on continuous assessment activities (15%), laboratory practicals (15%), and a written exam (70%).
